name: Howth Head Loop
description: North Dublin coastal loop around Howth Head. Punchy climbs, sea views, and a cafe stop at the summit. A Dublin cycling classic.

name: Dublin to Howth Head
description: City centre to Howth Head and back. Flat along the coast to Clontarf, then the climb over Howth summit. Perfect weekday spin.

name: Wicklow Gap & Sally Gap Loop
description: The classic Wicklow double-gap loop from Glendalough. Sally Gap's exposed moorland followed by the Wicklow Gap descent. Serious climbing.

name: Roundwood, Wicklow Gap, Blessington & Sally Gap
description: Epic Wicklow loop linking all the major gap roads. Roundwood to Wicklow Gap, across to Blessington, back via Sally Gap. One of the best long loops in Leinster.

name: Blessington Lakes & Glendalough Loop
description: Blessington Lakes to Glendalough via the scenic Wicklow Mountains. Rolling roads, reservoir views, and the valley approach to Glendalough monastic site.

name: Glencree & Sally Gap Loop
description: North Wicklow loop from Bray via Glencree and Sally Gap. Steady climb through the Featherbed, across the gap, and a fast descent back to civilisation.

name: Dublin to Glenmalure via Sally Gap
description: Dublin south to Glenmalure via Sally Gap and Glenmacnass waterfall. Remote military road riding with a dramatic valley finish.

name: Dublin to Wicklow Gap via Laragh
description: 100km day ride from Dublin through Laragh to the Wicklow Gap and back via Greystones. Classic south Dublin epic with 1,400m of climbing.

name: Blessington Lake Loop
description: Flat-ish loop around Blessington Lakes. Quiet roads, water views, minimal climbing. Ideal for a steady endurance ride or threshold intervals on the long straights.

name: Blessington to Glendalough via Military Road
description: Full day in the mountains. Blessington, lakes, Glendalough, Military Road, Sally Gap, Blessington, Naas. 100km and 1,400m of climbing.
